name: Churchable
shortDescription: A UK browser-based tool that turns uploaded sermons or sermon notes into clips, devotionals, study guides, downloadable resources and shareable AI-assisted pages.
suitableContexts: Churches repurposing sermons into short-form video and written material
Teams creating sermon-based study guides and devotionals
Churches wanting a controlled way to publish sermon-derived shareable pages

pricing.summary: Churchable publishes a free plan with two sermon uploads and a Co-Creator plan at £30 per month with unlimited video clips and content. The supplier advertises no card for the free route and cancellation at any time; confirm VAT, upload or usage limits and current commercial terms before purchase.

tiers.label: Free
tiers.detail: Two sermon uploads, sermon-transcript or notes-based content, video-clip tools, shareable page and PDF export, according to the supplier.

tiers.label: Co-Creator
tiers.detail: Unlimited video clips and content, team invitations and direct founder support, according to the supplier.

pricing.trialDetails: The supplier offers a free plan without a card; it is not described as a time-limited trial.

dataHosting: The supplier's privacy notice states that its servers are in Ireland. It also states that it may process information in the United States and other countries through third-party providers.
gdprInformation: Prompt Miner Ltd's privacy notice identifies it as controller for Churchable account and product data. It says user content submitted to AI features may be processed by third-party AI providers to deliver the requested functionality, is not used to train general-purpose AI models, and may include sensitive data if users choose to submit it. Its stated international-transfer safeguards and current processor list should be obtained and assessed before a church submits confidential pastoral, safeguarding or other special-category material.
coreFeatures: Sermon video, audio and notes upload
AI clip suggestions and transcript editing
Shareable sermon-derived webpage with AI chat
support: Co-Creator plan includes direct founder support

uk-operator.value: Churchable's licence terms identify Prompt Miner Ltd, trading as Churchable, as a company registered in England and Wales (15577817).

sermon-workflow.value: Supplier describes uploading sermon video, audio or notes; automatic transcription; clips; written templates; PDF export; and shareable pages.

pricing.value: Supplier publishes a free plan with two sermon uploads and a £30-per-month Co-Creator plan.

data-handling.value: Supplier's privacy notice states Irish server location, describes potential international processing through providers, and says user content submitted to AI features is not used to train general-purpose AI models.

editorial.assessment: Churchable is a specialised sermon-repurposing and communications product, not a replacement for a church database, live-streaming platform, safeguarding record or pastoral-care system. Its concrete UK legal identity, free entry route and published £30 monthly plan make it straightforward to evaluate. Because it accepts free-text and recorded sermon material for AI-assisted processing, churches should keep confidential pastoral and safeguarding information out of uploads and review the supplier's current processor and international-transfer information before wider use.
bestFor: Church communications teams turning a weekly sermon into several reviewed formats
Churches producing study guides, devotionals and sermon clips from existing material
Teams that want a free, limited practical test before subscribing
strengths: English company identity and current public licence terms
Published free plan and GBP paid plan
Sermon upload, transcription, clip, written-content and export workflow is clearly described
Privacy notice explicitly says submitted AI content is not used to train general-purpose models
limitations: Not a general sermon archive, church-management or pastoral-care system
AI-generated material requires theological, editorial and safeguarding review before publication
Supplier describes overseas processing through third-party providers, so current processor and transfer documentation matters
No public service-level or full retention schedule was identified in the reviewed material

procurementVerdict.problem: Turning each sermon into reviewed resources and communications without manually recreating every format
procurementVerdict.differentiator: A UK-operated workflow that combines sermon transcription, clips, written templates, exports and shareable AI-assisted pages
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Test one non-confidential sermon through upload, transcript correction, clip selection, theological review, PDF export and deletion request; obtain the current processor, retention and transfer documentation before expanding use
